Ontology_AssayAndWorkflow_prompt.notes: The experiment is a peptidomics study focusing on proteasome-catalyzed peptide splicing using synthetic polypeptide substrates. While PRIDE metadata lists 'Top-down proteomics', the methods describe a bottom-up-like analysis of digestion products (oligopeptides) using de novo sequencing. No specific PTM enrichments were used; the 'splicing' is a result of proteasomal enzymatic activity, not a standard PTM enrichment workflow like phospho or ubiquitylome. Acquisition is DDA based on the 'Top Speed' precursor selection description.

Ontology_ProcessingAndDifferential_promp.notes: This is a highly specialized experiment focusing on non-linear peptide sequences (spliced peptides). Standard bottom-up pipelines will fail to identify the spliced products as they are not contiguous in the protein sequence. The analysis requires a de novo sequencing approach followed by a custom splicing algorithm to map fragments back to the precursor polypeptides.
